scout.name: Pre-FOMC announcement drift
scout.source: Lucca & Moench (2015), Journal of Finance; Kurov, Wolfe & Gilbert (2021)
scout.claim: +49 bp in the 24 h before FOMC statements (1994–2011), fading to about +9 bp in 2016–19.

scout.name: FOMC post-statement drift
scout.claim: Gains right after the statement usually reverse during the press conference; declines extend.

scout.name: Press-conference fade
scout.source: Narain & Sangani (2026), International Journal of Central Banking
scout.claim: Powell-era press conferences are 3× more volatile and often reverse the statement reaction.

scout.name: Overnight EU-open drift
scout.source: Bondarenko & Muravyev (2023), JFQA; Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan (2023), RFS
scout.claim: ES 23:30–03:30 ET earned 7.6%/yr (2004–18); the NY Fed reports it vanished after 2021.

scout.name: Overnight drift after selloffs
scout.source: Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan (2023), Review of Financial Studies
scout.claim: The drift is strongest after RTH selloffs (negative closing imbalance).

scout.name: Month-end dash for cash
scout.source: Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen (2020), Review of Financial Studies
scout.claim: Selling pressure before the month-end settlement deadline, then reversal. Negative correlation in 25 of 25 markets.

scout.name: Dash for cash, long leg
scout.claim: The reversal days returned +103% cumulative excess in 2003–2013.

scout.name: 60/40 rebalancing front-run
scout.claim: When stocks are overweight vs 60/40, next-day returns are −17 bp. ES/TY Sharpe above 1 (uses bonds; NQ-only proxy here).

scout.name: Turn of the month
scout.claim: 0.15%/day on days −1…+3 (1926–2005); recent tests find it has faded.

scout.name: FOMC-cycle even weeks
scout.source: Cieslak, Morse & Vissing-Jorgensen (2019), Journal of Finance
scout.claim: Since 1994 the equity premium was earned in even weeks of the FOMC cycle.

scout.name: Large opening-move reversal
scout.source: Grant, Wolf & Yu (2005), Journal of Banking & Finance
scout.claim: S&P futures reversed large opening moves (1987–2002), but the edge was near trading costs.

scout.name: Option-expiration week
scout.source: Stivers & Sun (2013), Journal of Banking & Finance
scout.claim: High returns in expiration week as dealers unwind hedges (1988–2010).

scout.name: Pre-holiday effect
scout.claim: Returns before holidays were 9–14× normal historically; recent studies find it insignificant.

scout.name: Monday-open weakness
scout.claim: Monday's negative return accrued in the first 45 minutes (NYSE 1981–83).

scout.name: Macro announcement-day premium (CPI, jobs)
scout.claim: 11.4 bp excess on announcement days vs 1.1 bp otherwise.
scout.status: Needs the BLS release calendar (not in this data)
